params.body:
Three things yesterday taught the hard way, written down where the next reader will find them rather than left in a pull request nobody rereads:

- **A judgement reads the world after the change.** Two true claims were refuted seven minutes after their pull requests merged, against a reading from before the merge; and a second time against a reading that followed a redirect hop instead of the page behind it. Merging is not deploying, deploying is not measuring, and a judge is only as good as the reading it trusts.
- **A verdict can be withdrawn, and the withdrawal stays.** A ledger is not rewritten, but until yesterday it could not be corrected either, and one wrong refutation costs a playbook its rung for good. Every verdict a run was given stays on it with its evidence and the reason it did not hold; the run returns to unjudged. A person does that, with a reason.
- **A hand writes for how the thing it is fixing actually works.** One claim, three writers (Laravel middleware, a Netlify _headers file, nginx lines in a repo-carried config), and refusals instead of guesses. Writing the right thing in the wrong place is its own failure mode.
params.title: The paper carries what 13 September taught
